102-1: The 102nd term begins with Megumi Fujishima, a former child star forced into Hasunosora's boarding school by her mother, arriving resentful and disdainful of the entrance ceremony and the stiff freshman rep Kozue Otomune. While wandering, she meets the enigmatic Tsuzuri Yugiri, who declares she enrolled solely to become a school idol, and is later cornered by Sachi Ogami, the club's lone second-year, who drags her to the clubroom where Kozue and Tsuzuri already wait. A clash erupts between Megumi's professional pride and Kozue's dead-serious Love Live! devotion, though Tsuzuri quietly impresses everyone as a Kanazawa dance prodigy when they each perform. In the bath the two rivals share a rare vulnerable moment, and Kozue drags them into an all-night school idol video marathon that makes them miss morning assembly and earn a scolding—yet Sachi is thrilled to see her 'problem children' bond, marking the chaotic birth of the 102nd-term trio later nicknamed the Great Lotus Triangle.
102-2: A week into the club, Megumi grows increasingly drawn to the eccentric Tsuzuri, even as she keeps bickering with Kozue, and realizes Tsuzuri carries a deep sadness she calls 'rain in her heart' that never stops. Sachi announces a late-April live at the Music Hall; Kozue protests the three-week prep time, but Sachi insists showing the growth process is what being a school idol means, then unveils Hasunosora's three traditional units—Cerise Bouquet, DOLLCHESTRA, and Mira-Cra Park!. To the freshmen's shock, Sachi reveals she has already partnered with Tsuzuri to form DOLLCHESTRA, and since Kozue and Megumi refuse to work together, Sachi proposes joining both their units herself as a temporary bridge so the club can field all three.
102-3: Kozue reflects on how she dreamed of Love Live! since first grade and fought her prestigious musical family to attend Hasunosora, even as she grows frustrated watching Megumi's casual popularity at school. During practice Sachi trains all three units at once, revealing she is the chairwoman's granddaughter and a prodigy in her own right, but the tension peaks when Megumi suddenly stops coming. Kozue discovers Megumi watched her old TV show and realized the audience has moved on and forgotten her; devastated by the fleeting nature of fame, Megumi decides to quit the club and chase her old career, calling school idols a waste of time—until Kozue confronts her in the dorm, arguing that their bond matters more than any industry comeback.
102-4: On the day of the April debut, Sachi surprises the club with replica costumes of the legendary Dream Believers who once won Love Live!, moving Kozue to tears while Megumi stays cynical before admitting the quality. Tsuzuri stuns everyone with her natural stage presence at the Music Hall, where DOLLCHESTRA performs 'Sparkly Spot' and Megumi watches Sachi and Tsuzuri grow into a real unit. As Kozue's solo 'Reflection in the Mirror' approaches, Megumi feels creeping anxiety—but when Kozue freezes on stage, Megumi's support and the trio's trust pull her through, proving to Megumi that school idols can truly be the 'light' Kozue always believed in.
102-5: By mid-May Megumi has settled into the club, growing close to Tsuzuri (who now calls her 'Megu') and dropping honorifics with Kozue ('Kozu'). Recognizing her TV background, Sachi pushes her onto School Idol Connect (Suku-Cone) streaming; though Megumi mocks the low production, she finds her niche in casual 'zatsudan' talk streams and realizes broadcasting is a weapon to stand out from her polished peers. As the club preps for June's Nadeshiko Festival, Megumi's streaming confidence grows, and she begins bridging her old celebrity instincts with the amateur warmth of school idol culture.
102-6: In mid-June the Nadeshiko Festival prep consumes the club, with Megumi and Kozue developing a morning ritual to wake the oversleeping Tsuzuri. After Kozue's late-May birthday she has softened into a sisterly caretaker for Tsuzuri while Megumi handles her styling, and in the clubroom Kozue finally unveils the original song she has been composing—a 'beginning song' for the three of them. They divide the work (Tsuzuri choreography, Megumi costumes, Kozue music), with Megumi pushing modern casual looks against Kozue's competitive artistic pride, setting the stage for their festival performance.
102-7: With a week left, rehearsals for Kozue's new song crack under the weight of Tsuzuri's brilliant but near-impossible choreography, and Megumi snaps at both friends before storming out. Tsuzuri follows with hot cocoa—mirroring a kindness Megumi once showed her—and tearfully offers to dumb down the choreography, but Megumi clarifies her anger comes from her own insecurity, not Tsuzuri's talent, and refuses to let her apologize. Returning to the lesson room, Megumi sincerely apologizes to Kozue, and the three commit to performing the piece exactly as planned, their bond stronger for the fracture.
103-1: Kaho Hinoshita, a sickly child raised under overprotective parents, arrives at Hasunosora bursting with dreams of 'blooming' and big-city freedom, only to discover the school is a secluded mountain campus with strict rules and almost no access to Kanazawa. On the bus she meets the cold Sayaka Murano, and though Sayaka insists she wants no friends, the two bond over why they enrolled. Crushed by the campus's isolation, Kaho resolves to 'escape' and reclaim her freedom, while Sayaka quietly spots a School Idol Club advertisement that will change everything.
103-2: Kaho's escape attempt goes wrong when a school otter chases her and Kozue Otomune rescues her, then brings her to watch the School Idol Club perform with Tsuzuri Yugiri. The brilliance of the show awakens something in both first-years—Kaho sees the seniors as flowers truly in bloom, and Sayaka finds the inspiration she lacked. Moved, Sayaka formally joins and asks Tsuzuri to mentor her, while Kozue recruits Kaho to help with the club's upcoming live, pulling the reluctant freshman into their world.
103-3: After the student council rejects Kaho's petition for more shuttles to the city, she vents to her roommates and abandons an absurd mall-building scheme, realizing she must find fun where she is. Kozue recruits her to help stage the Welcome Live and names her temporary 'manager,' and during a dorm bath talk Sayaka reveals she is a figure skater struggling with expressiveness. Sayaka invites Kaho to join the club, but Kaho—still eyeing the transfer deadline—hesitates, torn between fleeing and staying.
103-4: As temporary manager, Kaho discovers Kozue is a multi-instrumentalist composing a new song and gives her heartfelt feedback that boosts Kozue's confidence. Swept into committee work and stage-building, Kaho reluctantly tries dance steps and unexpectedly enjoys the rhythm, and a phone call with her mother reveals her grim view of the school came from her mother's outdated stories. With the transfer deadline falling on the same day as the Welcome Live, Kaho begins to question whether leaving is what she really wants.
103-5: When her classmates find Kaho's transfer application, they offer bittersweet support for her leaving, but Kozue shares how her own musical family opposed her dream and urges Kaho to find her own reason to 'bloom' rather than take the easy path. Realizing she has been blaming the quiet campus for her own unhappiness, Kaho tears up the application in front of her friends, officially joins the club, and performs at the Welcome Live with Kozue—winning her friends over as fans and finally claiming her place at Hasunosora.
103-6: Kaho and Kozue watch Sayaka's figure-skating performance at the rink, where Sayaka publicly credits Tsuzuri for helping her find her footing and rejects the idea that she must choose between skating and idols. She calls Tsuzuri onto the ice for an impromptu live, the two reconcile their misunderstandings and name their unit DOLLCHESTRA, and Sayaka announces she will return to skating in ice dance—committing to a dual career with the skating community's support.
103-7: Kaho and Sayaka watch Rurino Osawa rehearse, but the mood sours when Megumi arrives and privately confronts Rurino for adding her name to the lineup without consent, accusing her of forcing a mentally and physically unfit dancer on stage. Rurino stands firm, insisting they perform together because she knows Megumi truly wants to return, and her words unlock a flashback of the two as children—Megumi telling lonely Rurino to watch her on TV—reigniting Megumi's buried desire to be on stage with her friend.
103-8: Rurino is wracked with guilt after realizing she never grasped the depth of Megumi's hidden struggles, especially when she finds the performance shoes she once gave Megumi worn to tatters from secret practice. Tsuzuri recalls Megumi saying she waited for someone to catch up so they could form an 'invincible unit,' and Rurino realizes she is that person; she finds Megumi practicing alone and declares she loves her for who she is, not her talent, and that her years in California made her strong enough to lead this time—finally giving Megumi someone to lean on.
103-9: After a chaotic but successful live, the exhausted club relaxes in a bath where Rurino's 'battery is empty' and Kaho and Sayaka marvel that the show worked despite the drama. Megumi uses the quiet moment to sincerely apologize for handling everything alone and causing trouble, shocking the first-years with her humility; Kozue, as president, forgives her lightly—saying only that she must answer her phone next time—which unsettles Megumi, who feels she deserves a harsher scolding for disrupting the team after a year away.
103-10: The club gathers as Sachi unveils the Second Music Hall, a state-of-the-art stage she spent a year building as a gift to her juniors—initially an apology for her perceived failures as the 'bridge' between generations, now a proud token of support. Kaho and Rurino are stunned by its scale and top-tier acoustics designed for safe performances, a gesture that deeply moves Megumi given her injury history. Sachi leaves the naming to the members, and the hall becomes the venue for their upcoming '150-point' song performance.
103-11: With Megumi fully back, the club prepares its first large-scale Kanazawa live with all three units, but Megumi frets over lax discipline and Kozue's lenient style, so she engineers a 'working retreat' at a luxury hot spring inn framed as a productivity competition. Her professional hospitality tricks are upstaged when Cerise Bouquet and DOLLCHESTRA excel through genuine effort, and the ruse is exposed when the members overhear her confessing the plan—yet the trip still yields a successful mini-live, and a promo video Megumi edits overnight goes viral, overwhelming the club with sudden attention.
103-12: The second-year trio meets to confront their past via the 'sapling certificate,' a non-interference pact signed after Megumi's injury and Sachi's departure; rejecting Kozue's attempt to shoulder all blame, they reconcile into the bond Kozue names the Hasunosora Great Triangle and submit a six-member Love Live! entry across three units. As they prep the Rindo Festival as their regional qualifier video, Kozue collapses from exhaustion, Sayaka steps in as acting president, and she, Kaho, and Rurino hit a wall securing a stage permit from the student council.
103-13: After advancing through the Love Live! regional qualifiers, the school prepares 'Open Campus' for prospective students, and Sayaka takes on heavy administrative duties that showcase her growth as a leader. Tsuzuri, feeling left behind, joins the Open Campus committee to prove she can contribute on her own; though Sayaka feels lonely as Tsuzuri rejects her help, Tsuzuri flourishes using singing and dancing to inspire others. When a rainstorm leads Sachi—now student council president—to consider canceling the finale, Tsuzuri confronts her lingering trauma over Sachi's cold departure a year earlier and, urged by Sayaka's trust, reconciles with her to save the event.
103-14: As the club preps the Hokuriku regionals, they're blindsided by a proposed 'internet ban' backed by a 'restricted' faction that sees digital distraction as harmful—a death blow since the club runs entirely on School Idol Connect streaming. With Sachi's council term ending in December, Kaho proposes a high-stakes gamble: perform the qualifier via remote stream and win using the very technology the school wants to ban, giving the permissive faculty leverage to overturn it. The crisis deepens when the administration imposes a data cap and an 'outing ban' blocking off-campus practice, forcing the club to fight for its very existence.
103-15: Following their loss at the Love Live! finals, the members return to Kanazawa each processing the defeat differently; Kaho and Kozue visit everyone, starting with Rurino, who feels like an imposter for joining late until Kozue validates her 'fun'-driven motive. Megumi channels frustration into ruthless competitive resolve, Sayaka hides grief behind disciplined routine, and Tsuzuri sits silently melancholic on the roof until Kozue helps her name her sadness as pride in Hasunosora and a 'greedy' wish for the world to see it. Reunited, the six resolve not to let the loss define them.
103-16: After the national finals loss, Kaho realizes she never thanked the community that supported them and proposes a 'Special Thanks' live to close the year—volunteering to write Cerise Bouquet's new lyrics alone to prove her growth to Kozue. Struck by writer's block and hiding her anxiety, she's rescued when Sachi invites her to hand-deliver invitations to local fans in Kanazawa, where Kaho learns the townspeople saw the loss not as failure but as a gift the club gave the city, refilling her resolve.
103-17: As Valentine's Day nears, Mira-Cra Park! splits over ideology—Rurino wants 'relatable,' comforting idols after a low-energy stream resonated, while Megumi insists idols must be 'dream-like' high-energy escapes. Megumi's jab at Rurino's shorter tenure sparks a fight, so Rurino proposes a 'shuffle unit' showcase; the lots pair Kaho with Megumi, Kozue with Sayaka, and Rurino with Tsuzuri. The other pairs sync instantly, and Rurino learns to blend her fun-first energy with Tsuzuri's eccentric calm, reaffirming their equal partnership.
103-18: As the year ends, the second-years—Kozue, Tsuzuri, and Megumi—write a new song as a graduation gift for Sachi to perform at the Renge Festival, dividing roles (composition, choreography, lyrics) and pulling their juniors in. Kozue reflects at her estate on how Sachi turned her from a rigid loner into a collaborator; Tsuzuri, walked through Kanazawa by Sayaka, embraces her place among friends; and Megumi, with Rurino, faces her 'black history' first stream and credits Sachi for giving her a new dream. Recalling their disastrous 102nd-term first meeting, the trio thanks Sachi for holding them together and delivers the song as a heartfelt farewell.
104-1: The new school year opens with Kaho oversleeping and rushing in, delighted to find Sayaka and Rurino placed in her same class as second-years. Self-conscious she hasn't 'grown up,' she adopts a stiff formal speech to look like a mature senior, amusing her friends who join the act. As upperclassmen, they discuss recruiting freshmen and their units' differing philosophies—Sayaka noting DOLLCHESTRA won't chase recruits the way Cerise Bouquet might—setting the stage for a new generation of club members.
104-2: Kaho arrives early to prep the club room and finds a first-year, Ginko Momose, standing reverently absorbing the room's 'tradition.' Fumbling a tea offer, Kaho learns Ginko's dream is Hasunosora and winning Love Live!, and when Ginko's notebook spills to reveal dozens of original costume designs, Kaho impulsively invites her to join Cerise Bouquet on the spot—an enthusiasm Ginko meets with a thoughtful 'I'll think about it.'
104-3: Kaho reports Ginko's hesitant reply to the seniors; Megumi teases her 'love-at-first-sight' approach while Kozue gently chides the suddenness but is pleased to have interest on day one. Kozue clarifies Ginko's unit placement isn't guaranteed—the three units each have distinct styles, so they must learn what Ginko herself wants. Inspired by Kozue's maturity, Kaho resolves to earn Ginko's voluntary choice by showing Cerise Bouquet's appeal rather than rushing her.
104-4: Kozue advises Kaho to mentor Ginko in her own way rather than copy Kozue's style, since Kaho will spend the most time with her. Kaho takes this to heart and is touched when Ginko shows a notebook meticulously recording all her advice, even as Ginko admits Kaho's energy is overwhelming. Ginko reveals she struggles to make friends her own age after growing up around elderly townsfolk, so Kaho decides to simply become her friend first and encourages her to join club activities at her own pace.
104-5: Kozue, Kaho, and Ginko set a live date as a concrete training goal, and Kaho enthusiastically invites Ginko into Cerise Bouquet—but Ginko asks for time, knowing the unit choice shapes her whole three years. Kozue agrees she only need decide by the live. Ginko grows comfortable enough to call Kozue 'senpai' and offers to help with costumes, revealing her family's crafting legacy, while Kozue gently tempers Kaho's wild stage ideas like a Kanazawa Castle replica.
104-6: On their day off, Kaho and Ginko walk the city, where Kaho admires Ginko's kimono style despite others calling her 'weird' or a 'Zashiki-warashi,' even confessing envy of her confidence. At a dyeing workshop tied to the Momose family, Ginko gathers fabric and embroidery tools and begins working, and Kaho watches in awe, calling it 'magic'—moments that let Ginko open up about the real motivation behind her enrollment.
104-7: By the lake, Sayaka and Tsuzuri reflect on DOLLCHESTRA's identity and what 'third color' they seek—Sayaka wants a 'hardworking' member who needs a place to belong. Their talk is crashed by first-year Kosuzu Kachimachi dramatically trying to 'cross' the lake and sinking; rescued ashore, she explains she ran from her mother's expectations and enrolled to stop being a 'nobody,' revealing her leap was a desperate bid to prove herself amazing.
104-8: Sayaka and Kosuzu keep trying to cross the lake, both ending up soaked, but the moment turns serious when Kosuzu realizes that if Sayaka does all the work for her, the achievement won't be truly hers. She insists on finishing it with her own strength, and Sayaka recognizes she was over-helping out of eagerness, apologizing and promising to cheer from the sidelines instead. Tsuzuri, watching, reassures Sayaka that overstepping is just proof she cares, deepening the bond between the DOLLCHESTRA seniors and their eager freshman.
104-9: Sayaka and Tsuzuri note the club is buzzing with recruitment—Kaho hunting for a Cerise Bouquet junior, Mira-Cra Park! seeking too—when Kosuzu appears and formally asks to join, pouring out that she's always felt like an 'extra' who failed at everything and believes this club can make her someone of substance. Tsuzuri welcomes her specifically into DOLLCHESTRA and Sayaka vows it will be where she belongs, giving the lonely freshman her place.
104-10: Megumi and Rurino wrap a Mira-Cra Park! livestream angled at recruiting freshmen; Megumi argues a bigger lineup means infinite potential, and Rurino agrees if a truly passionate candidate appears. Megumi's 'Operation Mero-Mero Seduction'—a literal basket trap baited with her acrylic stand—backfires comically when gamer Hime Anyoji simply lifts the basket and walks off with the merch, leaving Rurino skeptical and Hime's face oddly familiar.
104-11: After the trap fails, Megumi and Rurino fall back on flyers, with Rurino noting it takes courage to approach a popular club—and Megumi realizing she wants someone who reaches audiences they can't. Rurino then places the trapped girl: Hime Anyoji, the gaming streamer 'Tsumayou-ji' who won last year's student championship. Watching Hime's stream, Megumi is impressed by her professionalism and viewer engagement, sensing a recruit who brings something new.
104-12: Megumi and Rurino visit Hime, who is starstruck that her idols are in her room; Megumi cuts straight to asking if she'll become a school idol, and Hime confesses she's secretly wanted to for a while. She explains her gratitude to the game she streams—it gave her a place to be herself—and wants to promote it as a charming idol, the very encouragement (unknowingly from Megumi and Rurino) that pushed her to join. Megumi officially invites her into Mira-Cra Park!.
104-13: Kaho picks up Ginko, thrilled to see her making friends after classmates approached her because they saw her perform; Kaho vows to make Ginko's debut live the best ever, though her energy overwhelms the freshman. As they finish staging, Kaho reflects on her own first year under Kozue's patient teaching and tells Ginko to rely on her the same way—bonding the new senior and junior as Ginko asks whether Kozue was always so refined.
105-1: Ceras Yanagida Lilienfeld mourns the closure of her beloved Mizukawa school idol club, tearfully promising junior Kairi its spirit will live on, yet she arrives at Hasunosora brimming with excitement for a 'new world.' With transfer friend Izumi Katsuragi, she learns Hasunosora quit Love Live! to chase a new dream—absurd but intriguing—and Izumi reveals she came to stand where she was defeated in last year's finals, hungry for that passion. The two set the tone for the 105th term as outsiders carrying another school's legacy.
105-2: Ceras and Izumi tour Hasunosora's bustling, modern campus with the current members, Ceras awed that unlike Mizukawa it shows no sign of closing. Izumi adopts formal speech to honor the upperclassmen who gave her a second chance, eventually relaxing into rapport as Kaho cheerfully calls her 'Izumi-chan.' Amid lively first-year dynamics—Kosuzu and the others—the newcomers begin settling into a school at full capacity with new dreams to fulfill.
105-3: The 'Unit Experience Tour' starts with Cerise Bouquet, led by Kaho and Ginko; Ceras dazzles with a self-composed idol intro and boldly vows to 'change Cerise Bouquet from the inside,' revealing she's a capable songwriter—piquing Kaho's interest since the unit lost Kozue's composing after graduation. Ginko, struggling to stay serious under Kaho's teasing, nonetheless impresses the eager transfer with her poise as a new senior.
105-4: Ceras and Izumi visit DOLLCHESTRA, where Ceras delivers a marionette-themed intro and Izumi follows with a confident one Kosuzu admires. Sayaka shifts their talk to Omicho Market for a 'self-discovery' mission, explaining the graduated 'Hasuno Grand Triangle' set a towering bar—and that DOLLCHESTRA must now redefine itself without Tsuzuri's expressive power, pushing the current members to understand themselves before choosing a new direction.
105-5: At Mira-Cra Park!, the duo performs hyper-energetic intros; Izumi mimics Megumi's 'I love you all' so well that Hime mourns Megumi's absence with a framed photo, annoying Rurino. Rurino explains the unit's 105th-term pillars—broadcasting, exposure, social circle—to keep fans and distant Megumi encouraged, and Ceras, sympathizing with the pressure of graduated seniors, impulsively declares she'll join Mira-Cra Park! (though Izumi notes she's said that to every unit).
105-6: Ceras awkwardly practices calling Ginko 'Senpai' and coins the nickname 'Ogin-san,' endearing herself to Kosuzu and flustering Ginko. Kosuzu shares that Izumi has transferred into her class as a celebrity-like figure, and Ginko finds Izumi's aura intimidating—while Kosuzu notices Ceras grows more relaxed and genuine around Izumi. Their talk clarifies the two came to Hasunosora independently yet inevitably together, deepening their bond.
105-7: At the dorms, the seniors—Kaho, Sayaka, Rurino—struggle to compose songs for the 105th term's first Fes×LIVE now that their own seniors have graduated. Ceras offers her Mizukawa songwriting experience and notes Izumi can compose too, but Kaho politely declines, insisting this music must represent Hasunosora's 'now' and be made by the current members themselves. She playfully adds that if Ceras joins Cerise Bouquet, they'd gladly collaborate—keeping the creative reins with the club.
105-8: Ceras tells Kosuzu she'll join DOLLCHESTRA, wanting to repay the seniors through songwriting while staying in a different unit than Izumi to maximize her contribution. Sensing Ceras is acting from duty not desire, Kosuzu recounts how she nearly drowned crossing Hasuno Lake alone before Sayaka and Tsuzuri helped her succeed, urging Ceras to find a goal that truly matters to her rather than one borrowed from obligation.
105-9: Ceras confronts Izumi at night, admitting she once saw Izumi as a knight but now realizes she was a 'contract devil' who pushed her relentlessly—and Izumi coldly confesses she only stayed because she lacked dreams of her own and used Ceras to feel passion vicariously. Hurt that their bond seemed interchangeable, Ceras declares a new dream: make Izumi love being a school idol so their time becomes irreplaceable, challenging her to a one-year 'contract' and resolving they'll form a brand-new fourth unit rather than join existing ones.
105-10: As Starring Bloom opens and Kanazawa blooms with stages, Izumi tells Kaho a visitor awaits—Tsugumi Erikawa, who confirms she'll perform with her senior again. Though Tsugumi keeps a stubborn front and claims she still dislikes Kaho, she acknowledges the 'Power of Connection' and congratulates the club on reaching Love Live! finals. Kosuzu returns breathless, delayed because townspeople kept asking her for her signature 'Chest!' cheer, proof of her own growing bond with the city.
105-11: The club forms the Bloom Garden Party union to host Starring Bloom events nationwide, but members resign lacking confidence—so Kaho launches the 'Triple Flower Great Operation' as a visible model of blooming. A TV appearance, a walking stream through Kanazawa landmarks, and a pivot to save Hiromi's Omicho Market nodoguro surplus (via Ceras's song and a hero skit) prove Kaho can inspire real action, turning doubt into momentum.
105-12: As the fourth spring nears, the club prepares the Bloom Garden Party—equal parts festival and farewell—with the graduated 102nd-years (Kozue, Tsuzuri, Megumi) returning as alumnae. Though the seniors plan to stay background, the clubroom fills with nostalgia; Kaho builds the 'Album Tree' to preserve their shared history, while underclassmen like Kosuzu and Ginko fracture under the fear of inheriting legacies without their mentors, making the celebration as much about brave goodbyes as blooming.
102-8: The day after their successful Nadeshiko Festival performance, the trio celebrates with senior Sachi in the clubroom over their favorite drinks, their bond now effortless while Kozue still flusters using first names. Sachi expresses pride in the concert and a quiet wish to someday perform alongside them as a full four-member group, and reveals the student body has already nicknamed them the 'Great Triangle of Hasuno'—three first-magnitude stars (Kozue the musical elite, Tsuzuri the dance prodigy, Megumi the former star) whose combined light defines the 102nd term.
